newsitem.title: UK: UK to issue new clinical targets for the NHS.
newsitem.headline: UK to issue new clinical targets for the NHS.

text.p: Britain's National Health Service will in future be evaluated on the basis of how effectively it meets 15 clinical targets in addition to how well it satisfies budget and management goals, the government said on Wednesday.
"I believe that what everyone needs is reliable information about the quality, effectiveness and outcomes of care and treatment," Minister for Health Baroness Jay, said in a press statement.

Launching the government's hospital league tables for 1996-1997, she said the health service had for too long been judged only by management and financial targets. While this information remains useful, Labour wants to be able to tell patients and the public how effective the health service has been in delivering care, she added.
The new clinical targets will be published in full later this month and will be discussed with managers of the health service.

Among the things the government will be examining in future in judging the effectiveness of care will be data on the outcome of surgical procedures, such as the number of deaths that occur in hospital within 30 days of an operation or infections that patients incur following surgery.
"We need to produce information that is meaningful and useful, whilst at the same time taking account of the complexities of care clinicians face," said Baroness Jay.
